notes.title: One process routes everything
notes.text: libra-api mounts /webhooks, /v1 OTLP, /internal HMAC callbacks, /slack and /mcp, and starts the priority scheduler in-process. PR replay runs in a Fly microVM; Slack turns run in-process (stateless responder) or on the Codex worker.

notes.title: State: SQLite truth, ClickHouse spans
notes.text: SQLite on the Fly volume holds runs, jobs, incidents and ledgers. Spans go only to ClickHouse when LIBRA_USE_CLICKHOUSE=true. Scout candidates become signal_incidents before any Slack page. The Check Run is the PR artifact.

notes.title: Failure and trust boundaries
notes.text: Webhooks and callbacks are HMAC-verified; Slack signatures fail closed. OTLP returns 503 when ClickHouse misses the ack. Sandboxes get no customer secrets and stay read-only. LLM failures return unavailable, no provider switch. sendSlack blocks unproven claims.

views.title: Who talks to libra-api, and what comes back?
views.scope: Dashboard, coding-agent plugin, GitHub and Slack around the central API process

notes.title: Central coordinator
notes.text: Every surface hits one Hono process; see workflow views A (PR sandbox), B (detection) and C (Slack conversation).

views.title: A: How does a PR become an advisory Libra check?
views.scope: Webhook, gate audit, microVM replay, HMAC callback, Check Run

notes.title: Gates then dispatch
notes.text: Repo allowlist, draft, base branch and risk gates are audited; skipped PRs get no check. The VM runs build, tests, base/head replay and posts evidence back.

notes.title: Advisory and isolated
notes.text: Verdicts never block merge. Callback is HMAC-checked; writes are skipped unless the DB is provably local.

views.title: B: How do customer spans reach the incident store?
views.scope: OTLP ingest, ClickHouse ack, in-process scheduler reducer, candidate persistence

notes.title: Truthful ack
notes.text: Ingest authenticates the key, awaits the ClickHouse insert, and returns 429/503 with Retry-After rather than dropping spans. Readers filter producer_origin='customer'.

views.title: B (cont.): How does Scout decide to page Slack?
views.scope: Evidence reads from AWS and PostHog, LLM verdict, gated Slack post

notes.title: Page gates
notes.text: Pages need verified, fresh, active-entity impact; budget exhaustion falls back to deterministic copy. sendSlack enforces evidence and claim-grounding gates.

views.title: C: How is a Slack thread reply answered?
views.scope: Signed event, durable job, stateless responder or Codex worker, terminal reply

notes.title: Two responders, one job
notes.text: Each turn is a general_question job. Prod uses the in-process stateless responder; the Codex worker is the alternate and leases jobs without Slack or DB credentials.

notes.title: Terminal is final
notes.text: A send accepted by the host is final; ambiguous delivery settles as delivery_unknown and is never resent.

views.title: How does the separate Libra Logs product ingest logs?
views.scope: Customer log ingest into the isolated Libra Logs server and ClickHouse

notes.title: Isolated, card-gated product
notes.text: Logs has its own server, keys and ClickHouse; ingest is refused until card verification, and Logs ingest does not populate core PR-review traces.
